content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Junior Frontend Developer | React, TypeScript
Dublin, Ireland | aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404
GitHub: github.com/aiyana-bt-example | Portfolio: aiyana-bt.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Junior frontend developer with hands-on experience building web applications with React and TypeScript, including an accessible sea-swimming app with a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL database. Experienced with accessibility improvements, automated testing, and Storybook documentation through an internship and project work. Also builds websites with Next.js and Tailwind CSS.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
Backend and databases: Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL
Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma
Accessibility: WCAG 2.1, keyboard navigation, screen-reader testing, ARIA labels, colour contrast

EXPERIENCE
Frontend Developer (Part-time, Freelance) | Self-employed | Oct 2025–Present
- Built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, with class timetables and booking requests sent by email.
- Deployed the website on Vercel; content is edited in Markdown files.
- Completed small updates for two WordPress sites.

Teaching Assistant, First-Year Web Development Lab | Liffey Institute of Technology | Spring 2025
- Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development labs.

Software Development Intern | Harbourline Media, Dublin | May 2024–Aug 2024
- Worked with the web team on the company’s React news site.
- Fixed accessibility audit issues involving keyboard navigation, colour contrast, and ARIA labels across more than 20 components.
- Built a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery and documented it with Storybook stories.
- Wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

Barista (Part-time during studies) | Corner Bean Cafe, Dublin | 2021–2025

PROJECTS
Tidewatch — Final-Year Project | 2024–2025
- Built an accessible web app showing tides, water temperature, and weather for sea swimmers around the Irish coast.
- Developed the frontend with React and TypeScript, and a Node.js/Express API that caches data from public weather and tide APIs.
- Used PostgreSQL to store user favourites; used Chart.js for data visualisation and Jest for testing.
- Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100.
- Awarded 82% (First Class); demonstrated at the college project showcase.

Transit Delay Notifier — Student Hackathon | 2024
- Built the frontend as part of a three-person team that created a transit delay notifier in 24 hours.
- Team placed second in the student hackathon.

Study Buddy — Group Project | 2023
- Built the React frontend and login screens for a study-session matching web app in a four-person student team.
- Used Firebase Authentication; other team members developed the API and database.

EDUCATION
BSc (Hons) Computing – Software Development | Liffey Institute of Technology | 2021–2025
First Class Honours
- Final-year project: Tidewatch, an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers (React, TypeScript, Node.js).
- Relevant modules: Web Development, Databases, Human-Computer Interaction, Software Testing, Data Structures & Algorithms.

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Volunteer, Sea Swimming Club — Runs the club’s social media.

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Mandarin (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, well-structured junior developer CV with strong evidence of React, TypeScript, accessibility, Node.js, PostgreSQL, testing, Next.js and Storybook work. The Tidewatch project is particularly relevant and well quantified through its Lighthouse score, technologies, testing tools and project grade. The teaching-assistant experience also supports the role's mentoring expectations. The main content limitation is that the CV presents several academic and project-based capabilities alongside limited professional experience, while the target role requests a more experienced full-stack engineer. Some claims are broad: automated testing is stated, but only unit testing is evidenced; backend experience is present mainly through a final-year project rather than employment. No unsupported skills or experiences were detected when cross-referenced with the supplied candidate information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses conventional headings, simple text structure, chronological experience, explicit technology names and no apparent tables, graphics or multi-column formatting. Keyword coverage is strong for React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Jest, Git/GitHub, Next.js and Storybook. AI screening probability for this specific vacancy is moderate to low because several must-have terms are either absent or only partially evidenced: 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals/OWASP Top 10, and health-data privacy. The plain-text links should ideally be written as complete URLs, such as https://github.com/... and https://... , to improve parsing and usability.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with the patient-facing and accessibility aspects of the role. The candidate has built a wellness booking site, an accessible public-information application, React/TypeScript interfaces, a Node.js/Express API, PostgreSQL storage, Storybook documentation and accessible components tested with NVDA and VoiceOver. The candidate also demonstrates English fluency and some mentoring experience through teaching approximately 30 students. However, the candidate's material does not demonstrate two or more years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, OWASP/security awareness, or health-data privacy work. AWS/Docker, German/Croatian, analytics/A/B testing and NestJS are also not evidenced. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The remote preference and location may also be a practical issue: the candidate is in Dublin, while the advertised remote locations are Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia; the CV should not imply eligibility for this arrangement.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CHANGES
1. In the Professional Summary, make the distinction between professional experience and project experience explicit so the CV does not appear to overstate seniority. Replace the sentence beginning "Junior frontend developer with hands-on experience" with wording such as: "Junior frontend developer with professional internship and freelance experience, plus substantial academic project experience building React and TypeScript web applications. Built an accessible sea-swimming app with a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL database, and improved accessibility, testing and Storybook documentation during a software development internship." 
2. In the Professional Summary and the Tidewatch project, describe testing precisely as unit testing rather than implying broader test coverage. For example, change "Experienced with accessibility improvements, automated testing" to "Experienced with accessibility improvements and automated unit testing using Jest and React Testing Library." Do not add end-to-end testing because it is not present in the candidate information.
3. In the Study Buddy project bullet, add the supported authentication detail so the CV shows the closest available evidence for the security/authentication portion of the job: change the bullet to "Built the React frontend and login screens for a study-session matching web app in a four-person student team; used Firebase Authentication for user sign-in, while other team members developed the API and database." Do not describe this as OWASP or web-security experience, because that is not supported.
4. In the Technical Skills section, make the testing and accessibility scope more exact. Change "Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma" to "Testing: Jest, React Testing Library (unit testing) | Tools and collaboration: Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma." This improves accuracy and prevents an ATS or recruiter from assuming that Playwright or end-to-end testing is available.
5. In the header, convert both links into complete, clickable URLs, for example "GitHub: https://github.com/aiyana-bt-example | Portfolio: https://aiyana-bt.example.com". Retain the simple one-line contact format and avoid icons or graphics.

MINOR / OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENTS
6. In the Freelance experience entry, make the wellness relevance more explicit without overstating it. Change "Built a booking website for a local yoga studio" to "Built a wellness booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, including class timetables and email-based booking requests." 
7. In the Tidewatch project, retain the exact accessibility evidence but make the standards and testing terms more scannable by changing the final testing bullet to: "Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100." The current content is already truthful; this is only a clarity adjustment.
8. In the Experience section, keep the Teaching Assistant role because it is supported by the candidate information and relevant to the advert's mentoring requirement. Its bullet could be made more specific without inventing duties: "Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development labs." The current wording is already acceptable, so this is a minor refinement only.
